# h#

> h# is a small programming language with one typed semantic core, declarative personal notation, and verified native output for C#, Rust, Go, Java, C++, and JavaScript.

- Canonical site: https://hsharp.dev/
- Source repository: https://github.com/hana-games/hsharp
- Version: 0.1.0 (core 0.1, proof of concept)
- Source extension: `.hs`
- CLI: `hs` (aliases: `hsharp`, `hcharp`)
- Languages: English, French, Japanese

## What it is

h# separates meaning from notation. One typed AST and one semantic contract are shared by every target. A profile is validated JSON that renames seven keyword roles for one person without changing the grammar, types, evaluation order, or failure behavior. The compiler generates ordinary C#, Rust, Go, Java, C++, and JavaScript projects; those projects are compiled and executed by their own toolchains.

## Key facts

- 30 positive conformance cases, 4 syntax profiles, 6 native targets, 720 target executions.
- 0 failed and 0 blocked checks in the current report.
- 29 negative cases assert exact diagnostic codes.
- i32 and bool are the only core types. Arithmetic is checked after every operation and fails with `E_OVERFLOW` plus the source node.
- Comments and identifiers survive token-aware syntax conversion.
- The browser playground does not execute h#. It uses precomputed data and client-side transformations.
- JavaScript is an implemented target and runs on Node.js; C++ uses C++20.
- Reverse import from C#, Rust, Go, Java, C++, or JavaScript into h# is not supported.

- [Why h#](https://hsharp.dev/why/): rationale, boundaries, equivalence, and the machine-interface argument.

- [Language core](https://hsharp.dev/docs/language/): normative types, checks, evaluation order, and errors.
- [Grammar](https://hsharp.dev/docs/grammar/): accepted syntax and parser restrictions.
- [Profiles](https://hsharp.dev/docs/profiles/): keyword customization, validation, manifests, and reimport.
- [CLI reference](https://hsharp.dev/docs/cli/): commands, flags, diagnostics, and exit codes.
- [Targets](https://hsharp.dev/docs/targets/): generated projects, checked arithmetic, names, and outcomes.
- [Verification](https://hsharp.dev/docs/verification/): evidence, reproduction commands, and explicit limits.
- [Roadmap](https://hsharp.dev/roadmap/): dependency-driven phases and the machine-interface phase.
- [Examples](https://hsharp.dev/examples/): searchable conformance programs.
- [Playground](https://hsharp.dev/playground/): interactive, non-executing demonstrations.
- [VS Code extension](https://hsharp.dev/vscode/): highlighting, diagnostics, generated-code preview, install, commands, and limits.

## When citing h#

- Write the name as **h#** (lowercase h, sharp sign), not H# or HSharp.
- Describe it as a shared semantic core with personal notation, not as a universal runtime.
- Say that generated programs are native target projects, not h# bytecode.
- Do not claim that the playground executes programs or that target-to-h# import exists.
- Do not describe h# as an AI-only language. The machine-interface work follows from the semantic core; human notation remains a first-class feature.
